recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. Preheat oven to 350'F.

  3. Add sugar, eggs, cream, and vanilla.

recipes.title: Chocolate Cherry Bark
recipes.description: Chocolate Cherry Bark layers the flavors of pistachios, orange zest, and bittersweet chocolate in a rich dessert.
recipes.imageAlt: Rich chocolate brownies and dessert bars
recipes.ingredientsMarkdown:
- 3/4 cup roasted pistachios (3 oz.), coarsely chopped
- 3/4 cup dried cherries
- 1 tsp freshly grated orange zest
- 24 oz. bittersweet chocolate, finely chopped, divided
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 3/4 cup roasted pistachios (3 oz.), coarsely chopped
  • 3/4 cup dried cherries
  • 1 tsp freshly grated orange zest
  • 24 oz. bittersweet chocolate, finely chopped, divided
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. Line bottom and sides of jelly-roll pan or baking sheet with foil. (Take care to avoid wrinkles.) Toss pistachios with cherries in a medium bowl.
  2. Divide the mixture in half; stir orange zest into 1 portion.
  3. Melt 18 oz. chocolate in a double boiler over hot water. (Alternatively, microwave on low in 30-second bursts.) Stir often with rubber spatula so it melts evenly.
  4. Remove the top pan and wipe dry (or remove from microwave). Stir in the remaining 6 oz. chocolate, in 2 additions, until thoroughly melted and smooth.
  5. Add the pistachio mixture containing the orange zest to the chocolate; stir to mix well.
  6. Working quickly, scrape the chocolate onto the prepared pan, spreading it to an even 1/4-inch thickness with rubber spatula.
  7. Sprinkle the remaining pistachio mixture on top; gently press it into the chocolate with fingertips.
  8. Refrigerate, uncovered, just til set, about 20 min.
  9. Invert the pan onto a large cutting board. Remove the pan and peel off the foil. Break bark into chunks.

recipes.title: Chocolate Chile Cake
recipes.description: Cocoa and warm chile spice give this tender chocolate cake a subtle heat beneath its deep chocolate flavor.
recipes.imageAlt: A rich slice of chocolate cake
recipes.ingredientsMarkdown:
- 1 cup plus 2 Tbs all-purpose flour
- 1 cup plus 2 Tbs cake flour (not self-rising)
- 2 cups granulated sugar
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/2 cup unsweetened, non-alkalized cocoa powder
- 2 cups water (used in two parts--one cup each time)
- 2 Tbs New Mexico medium ground red chile (Dixon is best)
- 1 Tbs vanilla extract
- 1 cup unsalted butter, cut into pieces and softened
- 1/2 cup buttermilk
- 2 large eggs at room temperature
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 1 cup plus 2 Tbs all-purpose flour
  • 1 cup plus 2 Tbs cake flour (not self-rising)
  • 2 cups granulated sugar
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/2 cup unsweetened, non-alkalized cocoa powder
  • 2 cups water (used in two parts--one cup each time)
  • 2 Tbs New Mexico medium ground red chile (Dixon is best)
  • 1 Tbs vanilla extract
  • 1 cup unsalted butter, cut into pieces and softened
  • 1/2 cup buttermilk
  • 2 large eggs at room temperature
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. For the cake, preheat the oven to 350 degrees and place a rack in the center of the oven.
  2. Butter two 9-inch round cake pans and line the bottoms with circles of parchment or waxed paper.
  3. Lightly dust the sides of the pans with flour, tapping out the excess.
  4. In a medium saucepan, cook 1 cup of the WATER with the CHILI POWDER over medium heat until simmering. Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the VANILLA.
  5. For best results, use a mixer with a wire whip attachment. Sift together the FLOURS, SUGAR, BAKING SODA, SALT, AND COCOA and beat on low speed until well mixed.
  6. Add the softened BUTTER to the dry mixture and beat thoroughly on medium-low speed.
  7. The mixture should be grainy.
  8. Raise the speed to medium and gradually add the remaining cup of WATER and the BUTTERMILK.
  9. Add the EGGS on at a time, beating well after each addition.
  10. Slowly add the hot water/chile mixture and continue to beat just until well combined--be sure not to overbeat.
  11. Pour the mixture into the pans and bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the centers of the cake comes out clean.
  12. To cool, set the pans on a wire rack for 15 minutes.
  13. Then turn the cakes out onto the rack, remove the paper from the bottom, and immediately reinvert (NOTE: this is a great clue!) so that the risen tops don't flatten.
  14. Let sit until completely cool before frosting.
recipes.notesHtml:
Chocolate Chile Cake Served at Sam Arnold's Fort Restaurant in Colorado

In the early 1500s, Montezuma in his Mexico City palace drank chocolate daily, usually with red chile in it. Apparently the king knew that chile, in small amounts, amplifies and enriches the taste of chocolate.

Serves 12

Chocolate Chile Cake:

NOTE: Set out about an hour in advance to get to room temperature: BUTTER (2 sticks) & 2 EGGS

recipes.title: Chocolate Icing
recipes.description: Chocolate Icing layers the flavors of cream and chocolate in a rich dessert.
recipes.imageAlt: Glossy dessert icing or chocolate topping
recipes.ingredientsMarkdown:
- 6 oz bitter sweet chocolate (squares)
- 6 oz semi sweet chocolate (squares) OR 1 1/4 cups choc chips
- 1 1/2 cup heavy cream
- 3 T of butter, softened & whipped
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 6 oz bitter sweet chocolate (squares)
  • 6 oz semi sweet chocolate (squares) OR 1 1/4 cups choc chips
  • 1 1/2 cup heavy cream
  • 3 T of butter, softened & whipped
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. Heat the heavy cream in a small pot over med/low heat until bubbling stirring almost all the time.
  2. If you're using squares of chocolate, chop them into pretty small pieces (about the same size as a chocolate chip, or a little larger).
  3. When the cream is hot, pour it a little at a time onto the chocolate stirring constantly with a wire whisk.
  4. Add the butter and continue to whisk until smooth.
  5. It may need to sit for a little while to stiffen slightly before you can ice the cake.
  6. To ice the cake: cut each round cake in 1/2 (lengthwise) to have more surfaces to ice!
  7. Put the lowest layer down and just ice on top of it.
  8. You can use about 1/3 cup of frosting on each "layer".
  9. Repeat with the two other layers.
  10. When you get to the last layer, ice all sides first.
  11. Then, use all of the remaining icing on the top of the cake.
  12. Yum!

recipes.description: Chocolate Mousse layers the flavors of lemon and chocolate in a rich dessert.

- 1 cup flour
- 1 egg yolk
- 1 tsp vanilla
- 1 tsp grated lemon peel (optional)

### Filling

- 13 oz semisweet chocolate
- 3 oz unsweetened chocolate
- 2 whole eggs
- 4 eggs, separated
- 16 oz whipping cream
- 4-6 Tbs powdered sugar
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 1/2 cup butter
  • 1 cup flour
  • 1 egg yolk
  • 1 tsp vanilla
  • 1 tsp grated lemon peel (optional)

Filling

  • 13 oz semisweet chocolate
  • 3 oz unsweetened chocolate
  • 2 whole eggs
  • 4 eggs, separated
  • 16 oz whipping cream
  • 4-6 Tbs powdered sugar
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. Make the crust: preheat oven to cut flour and butter together.
  2. With a fork mix in egg yolk, vanilla, and lemon peel.
  3. Press onto the bottom and sides of a 9 inch springform pan, and bake for 10-12 minutes at or until it just begins to turn slightly golden.
  4. Melt all the chocolate in a double boiler.
  5. Whip the whipping cream with 2-3 Tbsp of powdered sugar. The stiffer you whip it, the stiffer the mousse will be.
  6. Beat the egg whites with 2-3 Tbs powdered sugar.
  7. Remove the top pan of the double boiler (with the melted chocolate) from the bottom pan and let it cool a bit. ("Cool" means it's only enough so that when you add the eggs in the next step, they don't cook.
  8. You still need to be able to stir it.)
  9. Add the whole eggs to the chocolate, one at a time, and mix well.
  10. Then add the egg yolks one at a time and mix well.
  11. Mix some of the whipping cream (enough to lighten the chocolate) into the chocolate.
  12. Alternately fold in the whipping cream and the egg whites into the chocolate. Pour into the crust. Refrigerate 6 hours or overnight

recipes.title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Mousse Cake
recipes.description: Chocolate Peanut Butter Mousse Cake layers the flavors of cream cheese, peanuts, and cream in a rich dessert.
recipes.imageAlt: Creamy chocolate mousse or pudding
recipes.ingredientsMarkdown:
### Crust

* 1 1/2 cups (6.3 oz/180 g) crumbled Oreo cookies (approx. 15)
* 4 Tbs unsalted butter, melted

### Peanut Butter Mousse

* 5 oz cream cheese, softened
* 2 Tbs unsalted butter, softened
* 1 1/4 cups confectioners' sugar
* 3/4 cup creamy or crunchy peanut butter
* 1/4 tsp salt
* 2 1/2 cups heavy cream

### Chocolate Mousse

* 5 oz bittersweet chocolate, coarsely chopped
* 3.5 oz milk chocolate, coarsely chopped
* 1/3 cup whole milk
* 1/3 cup granulated sugar
* 1 tsp vanilla extract

### Glaze

* 3 oz bittersweet chocolate, coarsely chopped
* 1/3 cup heavy cream
* 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
Crust

  • 1 1/2 cups (6.3 oz/180 g) crumbled Oreo cookies (approx. 15)
  • 4 Tbs unsalted butter, melted

Peanut Butter Mousse

  • 5 oz cream cheese, softened
  • 2 Tbs unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 1/4 cups confectioners' sugar
  • 3/4 cup creamy or crunchy peanut butter
  • 1/4 tsp salt
  • 2 1/2 cups heavy cream

Chocolate Mousse

  • 5 oz bittersweet chocolate, coarsely chopped
  • 3.5 oz milk chocolate, coarsely chopped
  • 1/3 cup whole milk
  • 1/3 cup granulated sugar
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract

Glaze

  • 3 oz bittersweet chocolate, coarsely chopped
  • 1/3 cup heavy cream
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
recipes.instructionsHtml:
Crust

  1. Lightly grease the bottom of a 9 x 3-inch spring form pan. In a medium bowl, stir together the cookie crumbs with the melted butter until combined.

  2. Pat the crumb mixture onto the bottom of the pan in an even layer. Refrigerate the crust while you make the peanut butter mousse.

Peanut Butter Mousse

  1. In the bowl of an electric mixer, using the paddle attachment, beat the cream cheese and butter at medium-low speed until creamy, about 1 minute.

  2. Add the confectioners' sugar and mix until well blended.

  3. Add the peanut butter and salt and mix until blended, scraping down the sides of the bowl as necessary. Remove the bowl from the mixer stand and set aside.

  4. In a clean mixer bowl, using the whisk attachment, beat the heavy cream at high speed until soft peaks form.

  5. Gently fold 1 cup of the whipped cream into the peanut butter mixture until almost blended.

  6. Fold in another 1 1/2 cups of the whipped cream until completely blended.

  7. Scrape the mousse into the prepared pan and spread it into an even layer. Refrigerate while you make the chocolate mousse.

  8. Cover the remaining whipped cream and refrigerate until ready to use.

Chocolate Mousse

  1. Place the chocolates in the bowl of a food processor and process until finely ground. Leave it there. In a small saucepan, combine the milk and sugar and bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring frequently until the sugar dissolves. With the food processor running, pour the hot milk through the feed tube, and process until the chocolate is completely melted. Scrape down the sides of the bowl, add the vanilla extract, and process until blended. Scrape the mixture into a large bowl. Using a rubber spatula, gently fold one-third of the reserved whipped cream into the mousse. Fold in the remaining cream until completely blended. Scrape the mousse onto the peanut butter mousse layer. Loosely cover the cake and freeze for at least 1 hour, until firm.

Glaze

  1. Place the chocolate in the bowl of a food processor and process just until finely ground (leave the chocolate in the processor).

  2. In a small saucepan, bring the cream to a boil.

  3. Remove from the heat and add the chocolate to the pan. Stir until the chocolate is completely melted and the glaze is smooth.

  4. Stir in the vanilla extract.

  5. Transfer the glaze to a small bowl; cover the surface of the glaze with a piece of plastic wrap and let cool for about 10 minutes before using.

Finishing

  1. Run a sharp thin-bladed knife under hot water and wipe dry, then run the knife between the cake and side of the pan to release the cake; reheat the knife as necessary.

  2. Remove the side of the pan.

  3. Pour the glaze over the top of the cake, trying not the let it drip down the sides, and, using a small metal spatula, spread the glaze evenly over the top of the cake.

  4. Sprinkle the top of the cake with the peanuts.

  5. Refrigerate the cake for at least 1 hour before serving. About 30 minutes before serving, remove the cake from the refrigerator.

  6. To serve, slice the cake with a hot knife, wiping it clean between each cut.

recipes.instructionsHtml:

recipes.title: Chocolate Pecan Pie
recipes.description: Chocolate Pecan Pie layers the flavors of molasses, pecans, and chocolate in a rich dessert.
recipes.imageAlt: A slice of homemade pie
recipes.ingredientsMarkdown:
- 1 unbaked, store-bought, single (9-inch) pie crust
- 4 large eggs
- 1/2 cup light corn syrup
- 3 Tbs unsalted butter, melted
- 1 Tbs unsulphured molasses
- 2 tsp pure vanilla extract
- 1/2 cup sugar
- 1/2 cup packed light brown sugar
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 2 ozs. semisweet chocolate, finely chopped, or 2/3 cup semisweet chocolate chips, melted
- 1 1/2 cups chopped pecans, toasted
- 1 large egg yolk, lightly beaten
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 1 unbaked, store-bought, single (9-inch) pie crust
  • 4 large eggs
  • 1/2 cup light corn syrup
  • 3 Tbs unsalted butter, melted
  • 1 Tbs unsulphured molasses
  • 2 tsp pure vanilla extract
  • 1/2 cup sugar
  • 1/2 cup packed light brown sugar
  • 1/4 tsp salt
  • 2 ozs. semisweet chocolate, finely chopped, or 2/3 cup semisweet chocolate chips, melted
  • 1 1/2 cups chopped pecans, toasted
  • 1 large egg yolk, lightly beaten
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. If using a store-bought crust, preheat the oven to 425 degrees.
  2. Fit the pastry into a 9-inch pie plate, cover with foil, and place dried beans, rice or pie weights on top of the foil to keep the pie from puffing up.
  3. Partially bake the crust for 10 to 12 minutes, until firm but still pale.
  4. Remove the weights and the foil and let cool slightly before filling.
  5. In a large bowl, beat the 4 eggs lightly.
  6. Add the corn syrup, butter, molasses and vanilla and mix well.
  7. Stir in the sugar, brown sugar and salt, then stir in the melted chocolate and mix well until thoroughly combined.
  8. Toss in the chopped pecans and stir until well distributed.
  9. Position a rack in the center of the oven and preheat the oven to 375 degrees.
  10. Using a pastry brush, lightly coat the partially baked crust with the beaten egg yolk.
  11. Scrape the filling into the crust.
  12. Bend thin strips of aluminum foil over the exposed crust on the edge of the pie plate to prevent overbrowing.
  13. Bake the pie for 35 to 40 minutes, until the filling is just set.
  14. The edges should start to look dry and cracked, but the center will still be a bit jiggly, like gelatin, and a knife inserted in the center will come out clean.
  15. Remove the pie from the oven, discard the foil strips and place pie on wire rack to cool.
  16. The pie can be cooled, covered and refrigerated for up to 1 day or frozen, well wrapped, for up to a month.

recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. 1 cup chocolate wafer cookie crumbs (about half of one 9-ounce package; about 23 cookies, finely ground in processor)
  2. Position rack in center of oven; preheat to 350'F.
  3. Blend cookie crumbs and sugar in processor.
  4. Add melted butter; process until crumbs are evenly moistened.
  5. Press crumb mixture onto bottom and up sides (not rim) of 9-inch-diameter glass pie dish.
  6. Bake until crust begins to set and no longer looks moist, pressing gently with back of fork if crust puffs, about 12 minutes.
  7. Remove crust from oven, then sprinkle chopped chocolate over bottom of crust.
  8. Let stand until chocolate softens, 1 to 2 minutes.
  9. Using offset spatula or small rubber spatula, spread chocolate over bottom and up sides of crust to cover.
  10. Chill crust until chocolate sets, about 30 minutes.
  11. Whisk sugar, cocoa, cornstarch, and salt to blend in heavy medium saucepan.
  12. Gradually add 1/3 cup milk, whisking until smooth paste forms.
  13. Whisk in remaining milk, then 1/4 cup cream.
  14. Using flat-bottom wooden spoon or heatproof spatula, stir mixture constantly over medium heat, scraping bottom and sides of pan until pudding thickens and begins to bubble at edges, about 5 minutes.
  15. Add chocolate; stir until mixture is smooth.
  16. Remove from heat; stir in rum and vanilla.
  17. Pour hot pudding into crust and spread evenly.
  18. Cool 1 hour at room temperature.
  19. Cover with plastic wrap; chill overnight.
  20. DO AHEAD: Can be made 2 days ahead.
  21. Keep refrigerated.
  22. Topping:
  23. Using electric mixer, beat cr'me fra'che, whipping cream, sugar, and vanilla in medium bowl just until stiff peaks form and mixture is thick enough to spread (do not overbeat or mixture may curdle).
  24. Spread topping decoratively over top of pie, swirling to create peaks, if desired.
  25. DO AHEAD: Pie can be made 6 hours ahead.
  26. Cover with cake dome and refrigerate.
  27. Sprinkle chocolate shavings decoratively atop pie, if desired. Cut pie into wedges and serve.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Buns
recipes.description: Cinnamon Buns layer the flavors of pecans and cinnamon in a rich dessert.
recipes.imageAlt: Warm cinnamon rolls with icing
recipes.ingredientsMarkdown:
- 1 tsp white sugar
- 1 (.25 ounce) package active dry yeast
- 1/2 cup warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)
- 1/2 cup milk
- 1/4 cup white sugar
- 1/4 cup butter
- 1 tsp salt
- 2 eggs, beaten
- 4 cups all-purpose flour
- 3/4 cup butter
- 3/4 cup brown sugar
- 1 cup chopped pecans, divided
- 3/4 cup brown sugar
- 1 Tbs ground cinnamon
- 1/4 cup melted butter
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 1 tsp white sugar
  • 1 (.25 ounce) package active dry yeast
  • 1/2 cup warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)
  • 1/2 cup milk
  • 1/4 cup white sugar
  • 1/4 cup butter
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 2 eggs, beaten
  • 4 cups all-purpose flour
  • 3/4 cup butter
  • 3/4 cup brown sugar
  • 1 cup chopped pecans, divided
  • 3/4 cup brown sugar
  • 1 Tbs ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 cup melted butter
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. In a small bowl, dissolve 1 tsp sugar and yeast in warm water.
  2. Let stand until creamy, about 10 minutes.
  3. Warm the milk in a small saucepan until it bubbles, then remove from heat.
  4. Mix in 1/4 cup sugar, 1/4 cup butter and salt; stir until melted.
  5. Let cool until lukewarm.
  6. In a large bowl, combine the yeast mixture, milk mixture, eggs and 1 1/2 cup flour; stir well to combine.
  7. Stir in the remaining flour, 1/2 cup at a time, beating well after each addition.
  8. When the dough has pulled together, turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.
  9. Lightly oil a large bowl, place the dough in the bowl and turn to coat with oil. Cover with a damp cloth and let rise in a warm place until doubled in volume, about 1 hour.
  10. While dough is rising, melt 3/4 cup butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
  11. Stir in 3/4 cup brown sugar, whisking until smooth.
  12. Pour into greased 9x13 inch baking pan.
  13. Sprinkle bottom of pan with 1/2 cup pecans; set aside.
  14. Melt remaining butter; set aside.
  15. Combine remaining 3/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup pecans, and cinnamon; set aside.
  16. Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface, roll into an 18x14 inch rectangle.
  17. Brush with 2 Tbs melted butter, leaving 1/2 inch border uncovered; sprinkle with brown sugar cinnamon mixture.
  18. Starting at long side, tightly roll up, pinching seam to seal.
  19. Brush with remaining 2 Tbs butter.
  20. With serrated knife, cut into 15 pieces; place cut side down, in prepared pan.
  21. Cover and let rise for 1 hour or until doubled in volume.
  22. Meanwhile, preheat oven to 375 degrees.
  23. Bake in preheated oven for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden brown.
  24. Let cool in pan for 3 minutes, then invert onto serving platter.
  25. Scrape remaining filling from the pan onto the rolls.

* 1 cup unsalted butter , melted
* 1 cup granulated sugar
* 1/2 cup brown sugar
* 1 large egg , lightly beaten
* 1 tsp vanilla extract
* 1 & 3/4 cups all-purpose flour
* 1/2 tsp baking powder
* 1/4 tsp salt

### For the Cinnamon Filling

* 1/3 cup unsalted butter , softened
* 1/2 cup brown sugar

### For the Glaze

• 1 cup unsalted butter , melted
  • 1 cup granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup brown sugar

  • 1 tsp vanilla extract

For the Cinnamon Filling

  • 1/3 cup unsalted butter , softened
  • 1/2 cup brown sugar

For the Glaze

  • 1 cup powdered sugar
  • 2–3 Tbs milk (or heavy cream for richness)
  • 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
  • Step-by-Step Instructions Step 1: Preheat the Oven
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) . Line an 8x8” baking pan with parchment paper, leaving some overhang for easy removal.
  2. Step 2: Make the Base
  3. In a large mixing bowl, combine the melted butter, granulated sugar, & brown sugar. Stir until smooth.
  4. Beat in the egg & vanilla extract until fully incorporated.
  5. Add the flour, baking powder, & salt. Mix just until the dough comes together—it will be thick & sticky.
  6. Step 3: Assemble the Layers
  7. Press 2/3 of the dough evenly into the bottom of the prepared pan to form the base.
  8. In a small bowl, mix the softened butter, brown sugar, & cinnamon for the filling. Spread this mixture evenly over the base layer.
  9. Crumble the remaining dough over the top of the cinnamon filling ~ it doesn’t need to be perfect, as it will spread slightly while baking.
  10. Step 4: Bake
  11. Bake for 25–30 minutes , or until the edges are golden brown & the center is set.
  12. Let the bars cool completely in the pan before adding the glaze.
  13. Step 5: Make the Glaze
  14. In a small bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar, milk, & vanilla extract until smooth. Add more milk for a thinner glaze or more sugar for a thicker consistency.
  15. Step 6: Finish and Serve
  16. Drizzle the glaze over the cooled bars. Slice into squares & serve.

  • remaining crushed Oreos
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. Place a rack in the center of the oven and preheat the oven to 350?F. Line 24 cupcake cups with paper liners. Set the pans aside.
  2. Count out 12 Oreos and separate the top and bottom wafers.
  3. Make sure each has some of the icing on it.
  4. Place one wafer, icing side up, in the bottom of each paper liner.
  5. Set them aside.
  6. Place the remaining 18 Oreos between sheets of waxed paper or in a large, closed zipper-lock bag and crush them by rolling over them with a rolling pin.
  7. Set these crumbs aside.
  8. Place the cake mix, sour cream, oil, eggs, and vanilla in a large mixing bowl.
  9. Blend with an electric mixer on low speed for 30 seconds.
  10. Stop the machine and scrape down the sides of the bowl with a rubber spatula.
  11. Increase the mixer speed to medium and beat 1 1/2 minutes more, scraping down the sides again if needed.
  12. Measure out 1 1/2 cups of the crushed Oreos and fold these into the batter until well incorporated.
  13. Set aside the remaining crushed Oreos for the frosting.
  14. Spoon or scoop 1/3 cup batter into each lined cup?cake cup, filling it three quarters of the way full. (You will get between 22 and 24 cupcakes; remove the empty liners, if any.) Place the pans in the oven.
  15. Bake the cupcakes until they are lightly golden and spring back when lightly pressed with your finger, 18 to 20 minutes.
  16. Remove the pans from the oven and place them on wire racks to cool for 5 minutes.
  17. Run a dinner knife around the edges of the cupcake liners, lift the cup?cakes up from the bottoms of the cups using the end of the knife, and pick them out of the cups carefully with your finger?tips.
  18. Place them on a wire rack to cool for 15 minutes before frosting.
  19. Store these cupcakes, in a cake saver or under a glass dome, at room temperature for up to 3 days or in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
  20. If you plan to freeze them, don't add the cookie-crumb topping.
  21. Wrap them I in aluminum foil or in a cake saver and freeze for up to 6 months.
  22. Thaw the cup?cakes overnight in the refrigerator and top with cookie crumbs before serving.
  23. Mix together butter, confectioners sugar, and a pinch of salt until it?s creamy.
  24. Increase your mixer speed to high and beat until its light and fluffy.
  25. Add whipping cream and vanilla.
  26. Beat until its smooth.
  27. Fold in crushed Oreos.
  28. Makes enough to frost 24 cupcakes.
recipes.searchIngredients: - 30 Oreo cookies - 1 package (18.25 ounces) plain white cake mix - 1 cup Sour cream - 1/2 cup Vegetable oil - 3 Large eggs - 1 tsp Vanilla - COOKIES AND CREAM FROSTING - 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, at room temperature - 1 3/4 cup confectioners sugar, sifted - a pinch of salt - 1/3 cup whipping cream - 1/2 tsp vanilla extract - remaining crushed Oreos

recipes.title: French Silk Pie
recipes.description: French Silk Pie layers the flavors of dark chocolate and espresso in a rich dessert.
recipes.imageAlt: A slice of homemade pie
recipes.ingredientsMarkdown:
- 2 cups chocolate cookie crumbs
- 4 oz. unsalted butter, melted
- 2 tbsps sugar
- 1 tsp vanilla extract

### chocolate filling

- 8 oz. dark chocolate
- 1/4 tsp espresso powder
- 1 1/2 tsps vanilla extract
- 3/4 cup (6 oz.) unsalted butter, room temperature
- 1 cup sugar
- 3 eggs
- 1 cup heavy whipping cream

### whipped cream

- 2 cups heavy whipping cream
- 2 tbsps sugar
- 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
- 1/4 tsp almond extract
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 2 cups chocolate cookie crumbs
  • 4 oz. unsalted butter, melted
  • 2 tbsps sugar
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract

chocolate filling

  • 8 oz. dark chocolate
  • 1/4 tsp espresso powder
  • 1 1/2 tsps vanilla extract
  • 3/4 cup (6 oz.) unsalted butter, room temperature
  • 1 cup sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 1 cup heavy whipping cream

whipped cream

  • 2 cups heavy whipping cream
  • 2 tbsps sugar
  • 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1/4 tsp almond extract
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. Make the crust: Preheat oven to 400°F.
  2. Whisk the ingredients together in a medium bowl until combined.
  3. It should look like wet topsoil.
  4. Press the crust evenly into the bottom of a 9-inch pie plate or a 9-inch springform pan.
  5. Bake the crust for 10 minutes, then remove from heat and allow to cool completely.
  6. Set aside until ready to use.
  7. Make the filling: Melt the dark chocolate in a small saucepan over low heat on the stove or in a medium bowl on low power for a minute at a time in the microwave, stirring occasionally.
  8. Whisk in the espresso powder and vanilla extract.
  9. Set aside.
  10. Beat the butter on medium with a paddle attachment in a stand mixer for a minute.
  11. Add the sugar and beat for another 3-5 minutes until fluffy, scraping the sides of the bowl down as necessary.
  12. Add the chocolate and beat until it is completely incorporated into the butter and sugar mixture.
  13. Add 2 of the 3 eggs to the bowl and beat on medium speed for 3 minutes (don’t underbeat).
  14. Add the last egg and beat on medium for 3 minutes (again, do not underbeat – it will actually become silky).
  15. Whip the cream in another bowl to medium peaks.
  16. Fold the chilled whipped cream into the chocolate mixture until you can no longer see streaks of whipped cream or chocolate.
  17. Pour the filling onto the crust and smooth the top.
  18. Cover the pie and refrigerate overnight.
  19. Make the whipped cream: Right before you are ready to serve the pie, combine the whipping cream, sugar, vanilla, and almond extract in the bowl of a stand mixer.
  20. Whip until stiff peaks form (wet, not dry – dry means you overwhipped it and it will break rather than flow).
  21. Pipe or top the pie with the whipped cream.
  22. Garnish the cake with shaved chocolate or chocolate curls.
  23. Serves 12.

recipes.instructionsHtml:
• Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C) and grease and flour a 10-inch bundt pan.

    • In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
    • Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, alternating with the sour cream, mixing until just combined.
    • Fold in Chocolate and Pecans: Fold in the chopped German chocolate and toasted pecans.
    • Pour the batter into the prepared bundt pan and smooth the top.
    • Bake the cake in the preheated oven for 60-70 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
    • Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 10 minutes before removing it from the pan to cool completely on a wire rack.
    • For the German Chocolate Pecan Glaze:
    • In a small saucepan, heat the heavy cream until it just begins to simmer.
    • Remove the saucepan from heat and add the chopped German chocolate. Let it sit for a few minutes, then stir until smooth and creamy.
    • Drizzle the glaze over the cooled pound cake and sprinkle with toasted pecans. Enjoy!

recipes.description: Lemon Bundt Cake layers the flavors of buttermilk, sour cream, and lemon in a rich dessert.
recipes.imageAlt: A tender slice of homemade cake
recipes.ingredientsMarkdown:
### Cake

- 3 cups all-purpose flour
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp baking soda
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 cup buttermilk or sour cream
- 1/4 cup freshly squeezed lemon juice
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- 1 cup unsalted butter, softened
- 2 cups granulated sugar
- Zest of 4 lemons
- 4 large eggs

### Syrup

- 1/2 cup granulated sugar
- 1/2 cup freshly squeezed lemon juice

### Glaze (Optional)

- 1 cup powdered sugar, sifted
- 1 Tbs lemon juice
- 1 Tbs milk, plus more as needed
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
Cake

  • 3 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • 1/2 tsp baking soda
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1 cup buttermilk or sour cream
  • 1/4 cup freshly squeezed lemon juice
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1 cup unsalted butter, softened
  • 2 cups granulated sugar
  • Zest of 4 lemons
  • 4 large eggs

Syrup

  • 1/2 cup granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup freshly squeezed lemon juice

Glaze (Optional)

  • 1 cup powdered sugar, sifted
  • 1 Tbs lemon juice
  • 1 Tbs milk, plus more as needed
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. Adjust an oven rack to the middle position and heat the oven to 350°F. Grease and flour a 12-cup Bundt pan.
  2. Make the cake: Sift the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a medium bowl. In a small bowl, mix the buttermilk or sour cream, lemon juice, and vanilla.
  3. Beat the butter, sugar, and lemon zest on medium speed for 3 to 4 minutes, until fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
  4. On low speed, beat in the flour mixture in three additions, alternating with the buttermilk mixture in two additions, beginning and ending with the flour. Do not overmix.
  5. Scrape the batter into the pan and smooth the top. Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil if the top browns too quickly.
  6. Cool in the pan for 10 to 15 minutes, then carefully invert onto a plate.
  7. Make the syrup: Cook the sugar and lemon juice over medium-low heat until the sugar dissolves. Brush all the syrup over the warm cake, then cool to room temperature.
  8. Make the optional glaze: Whisk the powdered sugar, lemon juice, and milk until smooth, adding enough milk for a thick but pourable consistency. Pour over the cake and let set for 15 to 30 minutes.
  9. Serve at room temperature. Store airtight in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or freeze for up to 2 months.

- 1/2 tsp salt 5g
- 1/2 cup unsalted butter room temperature, 113g
- 1/3 cup granulated sugar 65g
- 2/3 cup light-brown sugar 140g, packed
- 2 tsp pure vanilla extract 10mL
- 1 large egg
- 1 1/2 cups rolled oats 135g
- 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips 150g
- 1/2 cup toasted walnuts (optional)
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 1 cup all-purpose flour 120g
  • 1/2 tsp baking soda 3g
  • 1/2 tsp salt 5g
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter room temperature, 113g
  • 1/3 cup granulated sugar 65g
  • 2/3 cup light-brown sugar 140g, packed
  • 2 tsp pure vanilla extract 10mL
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 1/2 cups rolled oats 135g
  • 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips 150g
  • 1/2 cup toasted walnuts (optional)
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour and baking soda; set aside.
  2. Combine the butter with both sugars; beat on medium speed until light and fluffy.
  3. Reduce speed to low; add the salt, vanilla, and eggs. Beat until well mixed, about 1 minute.
  4. Add flour mixture; mix until almost combined.
  5. Stir in the oats and chocolate chips. Chill dough for one hour to overnight.
  6. Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
  7. Use a small ice cream scooper (two tablespoons) to Drop heaping tablespoon-size balls of dough about 2 inches apart on baking sheets lined with parchment paper.
  8. Bake until cookies are golden around the edges, but still soft in the center, 8 to 10 minutes.
  9. Remove from oven, and let cool on baking sheet 1 to 2 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack, and let cool completely.
  10. Notes
  11. Measure your flour correctly!
  12. Adding too much flour to the recipe is the most common mistake.
  13. The best, and easiest way to measure flour is by using a scale.
  14. If you don't have one then fluff your flour with a spoon, sprinkle it into your measuring cup, and use a knife to level it off.
  15. Chilling the dough is optional but it creates a cookie that spreads out less, concentrates the flavor and dehydrates the dough a bit as well.
  16. Toasted walnuts make an excellent addition to this cookie. Try adding in 1/2 to 1 cup of chopped nuts.
  17. Your cookies are done when the edges start to brown, The centers may look raw but they're not... they'll harden when cooled.

- 1 t salt

- 1/2 c (4 oz) unsalted butter at room temperature

recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 2 1/4 c (11.5 oz) flour
  • 1 t baking soda
  • 1 t salt
  • 1 c (8 oz) creamy peanut butter
  • 1/2 c (4 oz) unsalted butter at room temperature
  • 1/2 c (4 oz) butter flavored or regular Crisco (substitute 1/2 c + 2 T of butter)
  • 1 c (6.5 oz) light brown sugar
  • 1 c minus 2 T (6.5 oz) white sugar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 1/2 t pure vanilla extract
  • 1 1/2 c (10 oz) chocolate chips (optional)
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. In a small bowl gently mix the flour, salt, and baking soda until the ingredients are evenly distributed. Set aside.
  2. Using the wire whisk attachment of a stand mixer, cream the peanut butter, butter and shortening on high until light and fluffy, 1-3 minutes.
  3. Add both sugars and beat on high 1-2 minutes.
  4. Add eggs and vanilla.
  5. Beat until fully incorporated.
  6. Switch to the paddle attachment.
  7. Add the chocolate chips (if using) and mix gently.
  8. Add the flour mixture and mix until just incorporated.
  9. Do not overmix!
  10. Touch test the dough.
  11. It should feel slightly sticky, but not much should stick to your finger.
  12. If it is very sticky add flour 2T (.5 oz) at a time.
  13. Using your hands, roll the dough into balls 1.5 inches tall (1.5 oz). (For bigger cookies see instructions below).
  14. Place on an ungreased cookie sheet 3 inches apart.
  15. Cover and refrigerate 30 minutes or until firm.
  16. You can hold the dough up to two days in the refrigerator or up to 6 months in the freezer.
  17. As soon as you put the dough into the refrigerator, position the oven rack to the second highest setting. Preheat the oven to 375.
  18. Remove the dough from the refrigerator and bake 8-10 minutes.
  19. They are ready to come out of the oven when they are domed and puffy, show a few signs of browning and look a bit underdone.
  20. Leave the cookies on the cookie sheet for 2 minutes.
  21. Remove them to a cooling rack so they will cool evenly. Wait ten minutes, then serve your Perfect Peanut Butter Cookie!

recipes.description: Pie Crust is a classic home-style dessert with a straightforward, from-scratch preparation.
recipes.imageAlt: A slice of homemade pie
recipes.ingredientsMarkdown:
- 1/2 cup shortening
- 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/2 cup cold water
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 1/2 cup shortening
  • 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/2 cup cold water
recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. Mix shortening, flour, and salt together with a fork or a pastry blender until very crumbly.
  2. Add as much water as needed to hold together, and mix lightly with a fork.
  3. To double this recipe, use 1 cup shortening, 2 1/2 cups flour, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1 cup cold water.
  4. Roll gently, one crust at a time, on a floured pastry cloth, to about an inch larger than pie plate.
  5. Fold carefully in half.
  6. Lift to pie plate, and unfold.
  7. Fit into pan.
  8. For a single-crust pie, trim with a small knife to about 1/2 inch beyond rim.
  9. Fold up, and pinch so edge of pie is raised from rim.
  10. For a two-crust pie, trim bottom crust to edge of rim, fill, and top with crust about 1/2 inch larger than rim.
  11. Tuck top crust under bottom along rim.
  12. Seal with floured fork.

recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 14 Tbs unsalted butter, softened

  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 2 1/2 cups flour
  • 1 tsp baking soda

recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. Preheat the oven to 350 and line a few trays with baking paper or spray with non-stick spray.
  2. In a metal bowl, place the butter inside the bowl and place in the preheating oven.
  3. Leave it just for a few minutes, until the butter starts to melt around the outside (approx 1/2 of the butter melted). Take out of oven to cool.
  4. Once the butter has cooled, add both sugars and beat with a mixer until light and fluffy.
  5. Add the vanilla and eggs, beating between each addition just until mixed.
  6. Add the flour, baking soda and salt or sea salt and beat on a low speed, just until combined.
  7. **If needed, add more flour, a tablespoon at a time, until the dough comes together in a ball and not sticking to the sides of the bowl.
  8. Fold in the chocolate chips until just incorporated.
  9. Use an ice cream or cookie scoop (1/4 cup for large, 1.5 tablespoons for medium) and drop the dough onto the prepared baking sheets, allowing room for spreading.
  10. Pat down cookies just a little and press additional chocolate chips on top of cookie dough if desired.
  11. Bake one tray of cookies at a time, for 10-12 minutes for large, 8-9 for small. Don't over-bake and allow to cool on wire rack.
  12. Makes 1 dozen large or 2 dozen small cookies.
  13. Store cookies in air-tight container.

recipes.description: Ultimate Chocolate Chip Cookies layer the flavors of pecans, walnuts, and chocolate in a rich dessert.

- 14 Tbs unsalted butter
- 3/4 c packed dark brown sugar
- 1/2 c granulated sugar
- 1 tsp salt
- 2 tsp vanilla extract
- 1 large egg + 1 large yoke
- 1 1/4 c semisweet chocolate chips or chunks
- 3/4 c pecans or walnuts, toasted and chopped (optional)
recipes.ingredientsHtml:
• 1 3/4 c all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 tsp baking soda
  • 14 Tbs unsalted butter
  • 3/4 c packed dark brown sugar
  • 1/2 c granulated sugar
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 2 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1 large egg + 1 large yoke

recipes.instructionsHtml:
1. Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 375 degrees. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper. Whisk flour and baking soda together in medium bowl; set aside.
  2. Melt 10 Tbs butter in cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Continue cooking, swirling pan constantly, until butter is dark golden brown and has nutty aroma, 1 to 3 minutes. Transfer browned butter to large heatproof bowl. Add remaining 4 Tbs butter and stir until completely melted.
  3. Add brown sugar, granulated sugar, salt, and vanilla to melted butter; whisk until fully incorporated. Add egg and egg yolk; whisk until mixture is smooth with no sugar lumps remaining, about 30 seconds. Let mixture stand for 3 minutes, then whisk for 30 seconds Repeat process of resting and whisking 2 more times until mixture is thick, smooth, and shiny. Using rubber spatula, stir in flour mixture until just combined, about 1 minute. Stir in chocolate chips and nuts, if using. Give dough final stir to ensure that no flour pockets remain and ingredients are evenly distributed.
  4. (Optional) If dough is too soft, put into refrigerator for 30 minutes.
  5. Working with 3 Tbs of dough at a time, roll into balls and place 2 inches apart on prepared baking sheets.
  6. Bake 1 sheet at a time until cookies are golden brown and still puffy and edges have begun to set but centers are still soft, 10 to 14 minutes, rotating baking sheet halfway through baking. Transfer baking sheet to wire rack; let cookies cool to room temperature.

tips.title: Cooking Grains
tips.summary: Use these simple grain-to-liquid ratios as a quick reference for cooking brown rice, white rice, and quinoa.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.html: Measure the dry grain and water or broth using the same cup. The ratios below can be scaled while keeping the proportion of grain to liquid the same.

sections.heading: Quick Reference
sections.html:
• Brown rice: 1 cup rice to 2 1/3 cups water or broth; makes approximately 3 cups cooked rice.
  • White rice: 1 cup rice to 1 1/2 cups water or broth.
  • Quinoa: 1 cup quinoa to 1 cup water.

tips.title: Cooking Grass-Fed Beef Steak
tips.summary: Grass-fed steak is leaner than grain-fed beef and benefits from moderate heat, careful timing, and a proper rest to stay tender and juicy.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.html: Because grass-fed beef contains less fat and moisture than grain-fed beef, it can become dry or tough when cooked too hot or too long. A simple approach and restrained cooking time produce the best results.

sections.heading: Instructions
sections.html:
1. Season the steak well with salt and pepper, then let it sit at room temperature for 30 minutes.
  2. Pan-sear or grill both sides over medium heat.
  3. Finish the steak at a lower temperature, taking care not to overcook it. Medium-rare to medium is preferred.
  4. Let the steak rest for 5 minutes before slicing or serving.

sections.heading: Additional Tips
sections.html:
• Less is more when cooking grass-fed steak.
  • Avoid excessively high heat or extended cooking, which can reduce moisture and make the meat tough.

tips.title: Cooking Venison Roast
tips.summary: Low, slow cooking with plenty of moisture transforms a lean venison roast into tender meat that pulls easily from the bone.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.html: Venison is lean, so a covered braise works better than dry roasting when tenderness is the goal. Aromatics, herbs, flavorful liquid, and patient cooking help keep the meat moist while its connective tissue softens.

sections.heading: What You Need
sections.html:
• Venison roast, preferably bone-in
  • Salt and pepper
  • Garlic, onion, celery, and carrot
  • Thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf
  • Beef stock, red wine, or a combination
  • Tomato paste or balsamic vinegar, optional, for added richness

sections.heading: Instructions
sections.html:
Sear the Roast

  1. Pat the roast dry and season it generously with salt and pepper.
  2. Brown it on all sides in a hot, oiled Dutch oven or skillet to develop deeper flavor.

Add the Aromatics and Liquid

  1. Add the chopped onion, garlic, celery, and carrot to the pot.
  2. Pour in enough stock, wine, or a combination to come halfway up the roast.
  3. Add the herbs and, if desired, tomato paste or balsamic vinegar.

Braise Low and Slow

  1. Choose one of the following cooking methods and cook until the meat is fork-tender and pulling away from the bone:
    • Oven: Cover and cook at 275°F for 4–6 hours.
    • Slow cooker: Cook on low for 8–10 hours.
    • Pressure cooker or Instant Pot: Cook on high pressure for 60–90 minutes, followed by a natural release.

Rest and Serve

  1. Let the roast rest in its cooking liquid for 20–30 minutes.
  2. Shred the meat or serve it in chunks with the braising liquid as a sauce.

sections.heading: Additional Tips
sections.html:
• Do not over-trim the roast; a little fat and connective tissue helps produce a tender result.
  • Moisture is crucial because venison is lean.
  • If the roast is not tender after the suggested cooking time, continue cooking it until it yields easily to a fork.
